title: The Millennium floor — 11 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
The Millennium floor — 11 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the floor. 11 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 35 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 11. Most binding: span (7), isUnit (5), orbit (3), refl (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: flow.lean. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/index.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 11 sealed receipts fold to fa3e62be-f31f-8dd3-ac67-0dce4564fc6a. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (8, 3, 2, 1, 6, 3, 4). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: demand3.lean (3 observed, 0.85 expected, lift 3.51), address.lean (5 observed, 2.07 expected, lift 2.41), elementary.lean (9 observed, 3.9 expected, lift 2.3). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.18; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.56. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 22.5% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the structure underneath is standard and is credited. The doubling orbit 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 7 → 5 → 1 modulo 9 is the cyclic group generated by 2 in U(9), of order 6 because that is the multiplicative order of 2 mod 9; the units are {1,2,4,5,7,8} and the non-units {0,3,6}. Textbook abstract algebra, and treated directly in the literature on doubling maps modulo odd integers. Bounded, so the credit stops where the earlier work does: what is NOT prior art is the use of that orbit as a floor for what this deposit does and does not settle, which is a statement about this repository and has no earlier author. Verification by exhaustion in Lean is this deposit's contribution, and verification is not discovery. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. riemann_reflection_and_heart — (List.range 10).all (fun d => refl (refl d) == d) ∧ ((List.range 10).filter (fun d => refl d == d)).length = 1 record
  2. p_vs_np_inverse_is_unique — (List.range 9).all (fun d => ((List.range 9).filter (fun e => (d * e) % 9 == 1)).length == (if isUnit d then 1 else 0)) record
  3. navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded — ((List.range 48).map orbit).all (fun v => v < 9) ∧ (List.range 48).all (fun k => span.contains (orbit k)) record
  4. yang_mills_spectral_gap — (List.range 6).all (fun k => k == 0 || orbit k != 1) ∧ orbit 6 == 1 record
  5. hodge_span_is_the_units — (List.range 9).all (fun d => span.contains d == isUnit d) ∧ (List.range 9).all (fun d => isUnit d || ! span.contains d) record
  6. birch_swinnerton_dyer_vanishing — (span.foldr (· + ·) 0) % 9 == 0 ∧ ((List.range 9).filter isUnit).foldr (· + ·) 0 % 9 == 0 record
  7. poincare_single_closed_loop — orbit 6 == orbit 0 ∧ (List.range 6).all (fun i => (List.range 6).all (fun j => (orbit i == orbit j) == (i == j))) record
  8. the_seven_rest_on_one_finite_structure — ((List.range' 1 9).all (fun d => refl (refl d) == d)) ∧ (((List.range' 1 9).filter isUnit).length = 6) ∧ (span.eraseDups.length = 6) record
  9. the_three_non_units_are_exactly_the_unreachable — ((List.range 9).filter (fun d => ! isUnit d)) = [0, 3, 6] ∧ ((List.range 9).filter (fun d => ! isUnit d)).all (fun d => ! span.contains d) ∧ ((List.range 9).filter isUnit).length + ((List.range 9).filter (fun d => ! isUnit d)).length = 9 record
  10. the_origin_annihilates_and_never_joins_the_circuit — ((List.range 9).all (fun e => (0 * e) % 9 != 1)) ∧ (! span.contains 0) ∧ ((List.range 9).all (fun d => (d + 0) % 9 == d % 9)) record
  11. the_sequence_is_its_named_parts_and_closes — sequence = span ++ [3, 6, 9] ++ [0] ++ [1] ∧ sequence.length = 11 ∧ sequence.head? = sequence.getLast? ∧ 9 % 9 = 0 record
